'''David Kangas''' (DeckTech and Game Players Network handle '''Icebreath''')<ref name="dt-23975">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23975 QMC Clouds], DeckTech (David "Icebreath" Kangas, 16 June 2002). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/23975/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/23975/ GitHub Pages]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009092820/http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23975/ Wayback Machine].</ref> posted a [[Light Side|Light]] [[Quiet Mining Colony / Independent Operation|Quiet Mining Colony]] list on DeckTech (''QMC Clouds'') and published constructed lists on [[Game Players Network]].

Kangas began playing Star Wars CCG around 1997 and played both his first game and his first tournament in Salem, Oregon; in 2001 he turned to competitive play. When [[Decipher]] began forming the [[Players Committee]] in 2002 he volunteered, joined [[Shadow Squadron]] as Shadow 31 and began running his own events, about 20 in all by October 2004, including two mini-opens and the [[2005 Endor Regional]].<ref name="pcf-4063-55368">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55368#55368 State of the PC Address: So long and thanks for all the fish], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228234323/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55374%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

He finished 3rd in the PC's Winter Classic Contest, announced on 31 March 2003, as "David Kangas, Brush Prairie WA".<ref name="pc-classic03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030824053912/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/classicnews03312003.htm Classic Format Contest Results are In!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 August 2003.</ref> On 25 October 2004 he posted on the PC forums that he had resigned from the Players Committee and stepped down as Endor Flight Leader; he signed as "Formerely Shadow 31, Endor Flight Leader". The same post says [[Greg Anderson]] ran all three days of the 2004 World Championship and that [[John Hawkins]] had won the Endor Regional.<ref name="pcf-4063" /> He also quit the game, exchanging his collection, worth nearly $300, at Addictive Behaviors/CCG Obsession in Eugene, Oregon, for a box of [[WARS TCG|Wars TCG]] boosters.<ref name="pcf-4063-55368" /> Edward Fones, writing after the Endor Regional Weekend, thanked him for two years of running events in the area and said he had decided to retire both as a player and as a tournament director.<ref name="pcf-3974-55369">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55369#55369 From Rebels to Mavericks: 2005 Endor Regional Weekend], Edward Fones, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050224204234/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55343%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In November 2003 Kangas planned to restart his tournaments in Vancouver, Washington, at the start of 2004, after the closing of Tim's left no card shop in the area willing to support them; he was also promoting a second game, Ophidian 2350.<ref name="pcf-2442-37743">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=37743#37743 Looking for OR/WA players or tourneys], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (27 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323101525/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2442%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2442-37782">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=37782#37782 Looking for OR/WA players or tourneys], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (29 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323101525/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2442%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In January 2004 he wrote that the Portland/Vancouver area held at least one tournament a month, with about 6 players in winter and 8–10 the rest of the year,<ref name="pcf-2677-40034">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=40034#40034 Greetings!], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 January 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040309014208/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=40034%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and, signing as "Shadow 31, Ophidian Agent, Vancouver, WA", he and Edward Fones planned Star Wars CCG events at the GameStorm convention in Portland, Oregon, on 5–7 March 2004.<ref name="pcf-2668-39624">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=39624#39624 Star Wars @ GameStorm, Portland OR March 5-7], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 January 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318152649/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=40260%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
